brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: Single hex cell piece:0,0,0;full with top cover cover:0,0,0;full;top as dial face, wall-mount via accessory:0#0,0#1 hex-acc-keyhole on rear side flat for keyhole hanging.

Two props used as hands: prop:1 pencil (longer minute hand) and prop:2 pen (shorter hour hand) placed on dial centre. Configurator props are staging only and cannot be motor-driven; they turn only by user re-placing/rotating them. No mechanical clock mechanism exists in parts catalog.

Dial markers approximated by 6 inserts (insert:0,0,0;full;top;0/60/120/180/240/300) around face; combined with repositionable hands user can indicate time, but no accurate movement or numerals and no powered timekeeping. Material/timekeeping accuracy not verified by configurator (geometry only).

finish.summary: Built hex wall clock dial using one cell with top cover as face, hour markers approximated with 6 stud inserts, wall-mounted with keyhole hanger accessory, and two props (pencil and pen) as manually repositionable hour and minute hands. No powered clock mechanism is available in the Hex Cluster parts system; hands do not turn automatically.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
